subject: datastream
statement: The first eight bytes of a PNG datastream always contain 89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A; decoders should verify that all eight bytes are correct.

subject: datastream
statement: Although encoders and decoders should treat the length as unsigned, its value shall not exceed 2^31-1 bytes.

subject: datastream
statement: Chunk types are restricted to bytes 41-5A and 61-7A (A-Z, a-z); 13.2: the chunk type can be checked for plausibility. Reference: rejected as corruption.

subject: datastream
statement: Zero is a valid length. Reached for a zero-length chunk other than IEND.

subject: decoder
statement: A PNG signature mismatch, a CRC mismatch, or an unexpected end-of-stream indicates a corrupted datastream, and may be regarded as a fatal error. Reference: a chunk cut short by the end of the datastream is fatal.

subject: decoder
statement: A CRC mismatch indicates a corrupted datastream and may be regarded as a fatal error. Reference: fatal on a critical chunk, except PLTE in a truecolour image (dropped) and IEND (accepted), which 13.1 says can be ignored when invalid; those two warn.

subject: decoder
statement: A CRC mismatch on an ancillary chunk may be regarded as fatal. Reference: the chunk is dropped with a warning and takes no further part in decoding.

subject: decoder
statement: A decoder trying to extract the image, upon encountering an unknown chunk in which the ancillary bit is 0, shall indicate to the user that the image contains information it cannot safely interpret.

subject: decoder
statement: Encountering an unknown ancillary chunk is never an error. The chunk can simply be ignored. Under edition 2 this includes cICP, mDCV, cLLI, eXIf, acTL, fcTL and fdAT.

subject: decoder
statement: Decoders should not flag an error if the reserved bit is set to 1; it is sufficient to treat a chunk with this bit set in the same way as any other unknown chunk type.

subject: decoder
statement: Decoders shall recognize chunk types by a simple four-byte literal comparison; it is incorrect to perform case conversion on chunk types. Reached for an unknown chunk type that differs from a known one only in letter case.

subject: datastream
statement: cHRM, gAMA, iCCP, sBIT, sRGB (and in edition 3 cICP, mDCV, cLLI): Before PLTE and IDAT. A misplaced chunk is ignored (13.2).

subject: datastream
statement: bKGD, hIST, tRNS: After PLTE; before IDAT. Misplaced before PLTE in an indexed image or after IDAT: ignored. Before a suggested PLTE in a truecolour image: warned, kept.

subject: datastream
statement: pHYs, sPLT (and in edition 3 eXIf): Before IDAT. A misplaced chunk is ignored (13.2).

subject: datastream
statement: Chunks marked 'Multiple allowed: No' appear at most once; 13.1 names the presence of multiple gAMA chunks as a syntax error. The second occurrence is ignored.

subject: datastream
statement: If the iCCP chunk is present, the sRGB chunk should not be present, and the reverse.

subject: decoder
statement: Decoders shall not assume more about the positioning of any ancillary chunk than is specified by the chunk ordering rules. Reached for an ancillary chunk after IDAT.

subject: datastream
statement: The IHDR chunk shall be the first chunk in the PNG datastream.

subject: datastream
statement: IHDR: Multiple allowed: No.

subject: datastream
statement: A valid PNG datastream shall begin with a PNG signature, immediately followed by an IHDR chunk, then one or more IDAT chunks, and shall end with an IEND chunk. No image data: fatal.

subject: datastream
statement: IEND shall be last and its data field is empty; 15.3.1: no chunks or other content follow the IEND chunk. 13.1: most decoders can ignore an invalid IEND chunk; 13.3 acknowledges data after IEND. Data in IEND or after it is ignored.

subject: datastream
statement: A valid datastream shall end with an IEND chunk; an unexpected end-of-stream may be regarded as fatal. Reference: a datastream that ends cleanly after its image data warns.

subject: datastream
statement: All integers that require more than one byte shall be in network byte order. Reached for 16-bit samples.

subject: datastream
statement: PNG four-byte unsigned integers are limited to the range 0 to 2^31-1. Reference: an ancillary chunk holding a larger value in a four-byte unsigned integer field (cHRM, gAMA, pHYs, mDCV, cLLI, acTL, fcTL, fdAT) is ignored; for the APNG chunks the static image is decoded.

subject: datastream
statement: Pixels smaller than a byte are packed with the leftmost pixel in the high-order bits; scanlines always begin on byte boundaries. Reached for bit depths below 8.

subject: decoder
statement: When a scanline does not fill its last byte the unused low-order bits are not specified; a decoder cannot depend on them. Reached when those bits are nonzero.

subject: decoder
statement: Interlace method 1 (Adam7): seven passes; decoders are required to read interlaced images.

subject: datastream
statement: Filter type bytes are associated only with non-empty scanlines. No filter type bytes are present in an empty pass. Reached for an Adam7 pass of zero width that has rows (image narrower than the pass offset).

subject: datastream
statement: As 9.1#empty-pass, for an Adam7 pass with no rows (image shorter than the pass offset).

subject: datastream
statement: All the reduced images in an interlaced image shall use a single filter method. (Not emitted: IHDR carries the one filter method, so no datastream can violate this.)

subject: both
statement: Filter method 0 specifies exactly this set of five filter types and this shall not be extended; 13.1 names an invalid row filter value as a syntax error. Fatal in image data.

subject: decoder
statement: Filter type 0 None: Recon(x) = Filt(x). Reached when a scanline uses it.

subject: decoder
statement: Filter type 1 Sub: Recon(x) = Filt(x) + Recon(a). Reached when a scanline uses it.

subject: decoder
statement: Filter type 2 Up: Recon(x) = Filt(x) + Recon(b). Reached when a scanline uses it.

subject: decoder
statement: Filter type 3 Average: Recon(x) = Filt(x) + floor((Recon(a) + Recon(b)) / 2). Reached when a scanline uses it.

subject: decoder
statement: Filter type 4 Paeth: Recon(x) = Filt(x) + PaethPredictor(Recon(a), Recon(b), Recon(c)). Reached when a scanline uses it.

subject: decoder
statement: a is the byte corresponding to x in the pixel immediately before the pixel containing x (bpp bytes back, rounding up to one). Reached when Sub, Average or Paeth is used with bpp > 1.

subject: decoder
statement: For all filters, the bytes to the left of the first pixel in a scanline shall be treated as being zero. Reached when Sub, Average or Paeth is used.

subject: decoder
statement: For filters that refer to the prior scanline, the entire prior scanline shall be treated as being zeroes for the first scanline of a reduced image. Reached when Up, Average or Paeth starts a reduced image.

subject: decoder
statement: The sum Orig(a) + Orig(b) shall be performed without overflow (using at least nine-bit arithmetic). Reached when a sum exceeded 255.

subject: decoder
statement: The order in which the comparisons are performed is critical and shall not be altered. Reached when a tie between predictors of different value decided the result (pa == pc with a != c, or pb == pc < pa with b != c).

subject: decoder
statement: The calculations within the PaethPredictor function shall be performed exactly, without overflow. Reached when p = a + b - c fell outside 0..255.

subject: datastream
statement: The zlib compression method/flags code shall specify method code 8 (deflate compression) and an LZ77 window size of not more than 32768 bytes.

subject: datastream
statement: The additional flags shall not specify a preset dictionary.

subject: datastream
statement: Deflate-compressed datastreams within PNG are stored in the zlib format (RFC 1950) with deflate data (RFC 1951). Reached alongside the rfc1950/rfc1951 id that rejects the image data.

subject: decoder
statement: The zlib datastream ends with its Adler-32 check value; PNG does not say what a decoder does when the stream stops early. Reference: a stream that stops after the image data is complete (final block unfinished, or Adler-32 absent or cut) warns. A wrong Adler-32 is rfc1950-2.3#adler32. The same warning policy applies to DEFLATE/zlib faults detected after the complete image data, except that a wrong Adler-32 remains fatal.

subject: decoder
statement: Any RFC-conforming block shape decodes the same. (Not emitted: umbrella; the shapes are the rfc1951-* positive rows.)

subject: decoder
statement: IDAT chunk boundaries have no semantic significance and can occur at any point in the compressed datastream. Reached for image data in more than one IDAT chunk.

subject: decoder
statement: The compressed datastream is the concatenation of the IDAT data fields (noting that data fields may be of zero length). Reached for a zero-length IDAT.

subject: decoder
statement: As 10.2#idat-boundaries: an IDAT boundary between the two zlib header bytes.

subject: decoder
statement: As 10.2#idat-boundaries: an IDAT boundary inside the Adler-32 check value.

subject: datastream
statement: There may be multiple IDAT chunks; if so, they shall appear consecutively with no other intervening chunks.

subject: decoder
statement: Some images have unused trailing bytes at the end of the final IDAT chunk ... A decoder should ignore these trailing bytes. (Edition 2 is silent; both editions warn and ignore.)

subject: decoder
statement: An unexpected end-of-stream may be regarded as fatal: decompressed image data ending before the last scanline is fatal.

subject: decoder
statement: Decompressed data beyond the last scanline is not addressed by the specification. Reference: ignored with a warning.

subject: decoder
statement: IHDR is 13 bytes; for known-length chunks, such as IHDR, decoders should treat an unexpected chunk length as an error.

subject: datastream
statement: Width and height give the image dimensions in pixels. Zero is an invalid value.

subject: datastream
statement: PNG four-byte unsigned integers are limited to the range 0 to 2^31-1.

subject: decoder
statement: Valid colour types are 0, 2, 3, 4 and 6; an error is reported if an unrecognized value is encountered in the colour type byte.

subject: decoder
statement: Valid bit depths are 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16; an error is reported if an unrecognized value is encountered in the bit depth byte.

subject: both
statement: Only the colour type and bit depth combinations of Table 12 are allowed; PNG decoders shall support all valid combinations.

subject: decoder
statement: Only compression method 0 is defined. Decoders shall check this byte and report an error if it holds an unrecognized code.

subject: decoder
statement: Only filter method 0 is defined; an unrecognized value is reported as an error.

subject: decoder
statement: Interlace method is 0 or 1; an unrecognized value is reported as an error.

subject: decoder
statement: Decoders support every valid combination: greyscale (colour type 0) at bit depth 1. Reached for such an IHDR.

subject: decoder
statement: Decoders support every valid combination: greyscale (colour type 0) at bit depth 2. Reached for such an IHDR.

subject: decoder
statement: Decoders support every valid combination: greyscale (colour type 0) at bit depth 4. Reached for such an IHDR.

subject: decoder
statement: Decoders support every valid combination: greyscale (colour type 0) at bit depth 8. Reached for such an IHDR.

subject: decoder
statement: Decoders support every valid combination: greyscale (colour type 0) at bit depth 16. Reached for such an IHDR.

subject: decoder
statement: Decoders support every valid combination: truecolour (colour type 2) at bit depth 8. Reached for such an IHDR.

subject: decoder
statement: Decoders support every valid combination: truecolour (colour type 2) at bit depth 16. Reached for such an IHDR.

subject: decoder
statement: Decoders support every valid combination: indexed-colour (colour type 3) at bit depth 1. Reached for such an IHDR.

subject: decoder
statement: Decoders support every valid combination: indexed-colour (colour type 3) at bit depth 2. Reached for such an IHDR.

subject: decoder
statement: Decoders support every valid combination: indexed-colour (colour type 3) at bit depth 4. Reached for such an IHDR.

subject: decoder
statement: Decoders support every valid combination: indexed-colour (colour type 3) at bit depth 8. Reached for such an IHDR.

subject: decoder
statement: Decoders support every valid combination: greyscale with alpha (colour type 4) at bit depth 8. Reached for such an IHDR.

subject: decoder
statement: Decoders support every valid combination: greyscale with alpha (colour type 4) at bit depth 16. Reached for such an IHDR.

subject: decoder
statement: Decoders support every valid combination: truecolour with alpha (colour type 6) at bit depth 8. Reached for such an IHDR.

subject: decoder
statement: Decoders support every valid combination: truecolour with alpha (colour type 6) at bit depth 16. Reached for such an IHDR.

subject: datastream
statement: Colour type 3: each pixel is a palette index; a PLTE chunk shall appear, before the first IDAT.

subject: datastream
statement: PLTE holds 1 to 256 entries; a chunk length not divisible by 3 is an error. 13.1: an image viewer cannot recover from an empty PLTE chunk in an indexed image.

subject: datastream
statement: 13.1: an image viewer can ignore an invalid PLTE chunk in a truecolour image (invalid length, or after IDAT).

subject: datastream
statement: PLTE shall not appear for colour types 0 and 4. Reference: ignored with a warning.

subject: datastream
statement: There shall not be more than one PLTE chunk. Reference: fatal for colour type 3, ignored with a warning for a suggested palette.

subject: datastream
statement: The number of palette entries shall not exceed the range that can be represented in the image bit depth. Reference: warning; the surplus entries are unreachable.

subject: datastream
statement: It is permissible to have fewer entries than the bit depth would allow. Reached for such a palette.

subject: datastream
statement: For colour types 2 and 6 the PLTE chunk is optional; if present it provides a suggested set of colours and does not affect decoding.

subject: both
statement: Edition 2: any out-of-range pixel value found in the image data is an error; 13.3 says unexpected values shall be treated as errors and recommends fatal errors in critical chunks. Reference: rejected. (Edition 3 instead requires opaque black: 13.1#index-opaque-black.)

subject: decoder
statement: Edition 3: any out-of-range pixel value is an error; if out-of-range indexes are encountered, displaying the pixel as opaque black is now required.

subject: datastream
statement: A tRNS chunk shall not appear for colour types 4 and 6, since a full alpha channel is already present. Ignored.

subject: datastream
statement: tRNS is 2 bytes for colour type 0 and 6 for type 2; for type 3 it shall not contain more alpha values than there are palette entries. Ignored.

subject: datastream
statement: A tRNS chunk may contain fewer values than there are palette entries; the alpha value for all remaining palette entries is assumed to be 255. (Zero values is fewer and is accepted.)

subject: decoder
statement: If the image bit depth is less than 16, the least significant bits are used. Encoders should set the other bits to 0, and decoders must mask the other bits to 0 before the value is used. Reached for a tRNS sample with bits above the bit depth. Edition 2: "the least significant bits are used and the others are 0", read as the same instruction.

subject: decoder
statement: Pixels of the specified grey or RGB sample value are treated as transparent (alpha 0), all others fully opaque; palette pixels take the tRNS alpha of their index. Reached when tRNS makes at least one pixel non-opaque.

subject: decoder
statement: When processing 16-bit greyscale or truecolour data in the tRNS chunk, both bytes of the sample values are evaluated to determine whether a pixel is transparent.

subject: decoder
statement: When comparing pixel values to tRNS chunk values to detect transparent pixels, the comparison shall be done exactly, before any rescaling. Reached for tRNS on greyscale below 8 bits.

subject: decoder
statement: For known-length chunks, decoders should treat an unexpected chunk length as an error; an unexpected value in an ancillary chunk can be handled by ignoring the whole chunk (cHRM 32, gAMA 4, sRGB 1, cICP 4, mDCV 24, cLLI 8, pHYs 9, tIME 7; sBIT and bKGD by colour type).

subject: datastream
statement: cHRM: eight four-byte chromaticity values. Reached for a well-formed cHRM.

subject: datastream
statement: gAMA: the gamma value times 100000. Reached for a well-formed gAMA.

subject: decoder
statement: A gAMA chunk containing zero is meaningless but could appear by mistake. Decoders should ignore it.

subject: datastream
statement: iCCP: profile name, null, compression method 0, zlib-compressed ICC profile. Reached for a well-formed iCCP.

subject: datastream
statement: iCCP: Profile name 1-79 bytes, Null separator, Compression method 1 byte, Compressed profile. Missing separator or method byte: ignored.

subject: datastream
statement: The only compression method defined in this specification is method 0. Ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: The compressed profile is a zlib datastream with deflate compression (RFC 1950/1951, checked by inflate.py); invalid, truncated or followed by extra bytes: ignored.

subject: datastream
statement: Decompression of this datastream yields the embedded ICC profile (ICC.1): the header's profile size equals the profile's, the file signature is acsp, and the tag table and every tag's data lie within the profile. Reference: ignored otherwise; tag contents are not examined.

subject: datastream
statement: The colour space of the ICC profile shall be an RGB colour space for colour images (colour types 2, 3 and 6), or a greyscale colour space for greyscale images (colour types 0 and 4). Checked on the ICC header colour space signature; ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: sBIT: one byte per channel. Reached for a well-formed sBIT.

subject: datastream
statement: Each depth specified in sBIT shall be greater than zero and less than or equal to the sample depth (which is 8 for indexed-colour images, and the bit depth given in IHDR for other colour types). Ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: sRGB: one byte, rendering intent. Reached for a well-formed sRGB.

subject: datastream
statement: Rendering intent: only the values 0 to 3 shall be used. Ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: A gAMA or cHRM written with sRGB: only the values of Table 17 shall be used (gAMA 45455; cHRM 31270 32900 64000 33000 30000 60000 15000 6000). Decoders that use sRGB ignore both chunks.

subject: datastream
statement: cICP: colour primaries, transfer function, matrix coefficients, video full range flag. Reached for a well-formed cICP.

subject: datastream
statement: RGB is currently the only supported colour model in PNG, and as such Matrix Coefficients shall be set to 0. Ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: Each field corresponds to the parameter of the same name in ITU-T H.273, where VideoFullRangeFlag is a one-bit flag (0 or 1). Ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: mDCV: 24 bytes of mastering display colour volume. Reached for a well-formed mDCV.

subject: datastream
statement: A cICP chunk must accompany the use of mDCV in order to establish the basic characteristics of the image content.

subject: datastream
statement: cLLI: MaxCLL and MaxFALL, four bytes each. Reached for a well-formed cLLI.

subject: datastream
statement: Keywords are restricted to 1 to 79 bytes in length (also iCCP profile names and sPLT palette names). The chunk is ignored.

subject: datastream
statement: Keywords shall contain only printable Latin-1 characters and spaces; that is, only code points 0x20-7E and 0xA1-FF are allowed (also iCCP profile names and sPLT palette names). The chunk is ignored.

subject: datastream
statement: Leading spaces, trailing spaces, and consecutive spaces are not permitted in keywords (also iCCP profile names and sPLT palette names). The chunk is ignored.

subject: datastream
statement: tEXt: keyword, null separator, Latin-1 text. Reached for a well-formed tEXt.

subject: datastream
statement: The keyword and text string are separated by a zero byte (null character). Ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: Neither the keyword nor the text string may contain a null character. Ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: tEXt and zTXt content is restricted to the printable Latin-1 character set plus U+000A LINE FEED (edition 2: the Latin-1 character set plus the linefeed character); checked as 0A, 20-7E, A0-FF. Ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: zTXt: keyword, null, compression method 0, zlib-compressed Latin-1 text. Reached for a well-formed zTXt.

subject: datastream
statement: zTXt: Keyword 1-79 bytes, Null separator, Compression method 1 byte, Compressed text datastream. Missing separator or method byte: ignored.

subject: datastream
statement: The only compression method value defined is 0 (deflate compression). Ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: The compressed text is a zlib datastream with deflate compression (checked by inflate.py); invalid, truncated or followed by extra bytes: ignored.

subject: datastream
statement: Decompression yields text identical to that of an equivalent tEXt chunk, which may not contain a null character. Ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: As 11.3.3.2#latin1, for the decompressed zTXt text.

subject: datastream
statement: iTXt: keyword, null, compression flag, compression method, language tag, null, translated keyword, null, UTF-8 text. Reached for a well-formed iTXt.

subject: datastream
statement: iTXt holds a keyword and null separator, compression flag and method bytes, then a language tag and translated keyword each ended by a null separator. Missing: ignored.

subject: datastream
statement: The compression flag is 0 for uncompressed text, 1 for compressed text. Ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: For compressed text, the only compression method defined is 0. Ignored otherwise.

subject: decoder
statement: For uncompressed text, encoders shall set the compression method to 0, and decoders shall ignore it. Reached for an uncompressed iTXt with a nonzero method byte.

subject: datastream
statement: The language tag is a well-formed language tag: edition 3 BCP 47 (RFC 5646 2.1 ABNF, including the grandfathered tags), edition 2 RFC 3066 (a 1-8 letter primary subtag, then 1-8 letter-or-digit subtags). Registry membership is not checked. Reference: the chunk is ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: Compressed iTXt text is a zlib datastream with deflate compression (checked by inflate.py); invalid, truncated or followed by extra bytes: ignored.

subject: datastream
statement: The translated keyword and text both use the UTF-8 encoding (RFC 3629). Ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: Neither the translated keyword nor the text shall contain a zero byte (null character). Ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: bKGD: 2, 6 or 1 bytes by colour type. Reached for a well-formed bKGD.

subject: datastream
statement: For colour type 3, the value is the palette index of the colour to be used as background; an index past the palette is ignored.

subject: decoder
statement: If the image bit depth is less than 16, the least significant bits are used. Encoders should set the other bits to 0, and decoders must mask the other bits to 0 before the value is used. Reached for a bKGD sample with bits above the bit depth. Edition 2: "the least significant bits are used and the others are 0", read as the same instruction.

subject: datastream
statement: hIST: one two-byte frequency per palette entry. Reached for a well-formed hIST.

subject: datastream
statement: There shall be exactly one entry for each entry in the PLTE chunk. Ignored otherwise (including when there is no PLTE).

subject: datastream
statement: A histogram entry shall be nonzero if there are any pixels of that colour. Checked for colour type 3 after decoding.

subject: datastream
statement: pHYs: pixels per unit X and Y, unit specifier. Reached for a well-formed pHYs.

subject: datastream
statement: Unit specifier values: 0 unit is unknown, 1 unit is the metre. Ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: sPLT: palette name, null, sample depth, entries. Reached for a well-formed sPLT.

subject: datastream
statement: sPLT: Palette name 1-79 bytes, Null separator, Sample depth 1 byte, entries. Missing separator or depth byte: ignored.

subject: datastream
statement: Multiple sPLT chunks are permitted, but each shall have a different palette name. The later chunk is ignored.

subject: datastream
statement: The sPLT sample depth shall be 8 or 16. Ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: The length after the sample depth byte shall be divisible by 6 if the sPLT sample depth is 8, or by 10 if it is 16. Ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: Entries shall appear in decreasing order of frequency (equal frequencies accepted). Ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: eXIf: an Exif profile (TIFF structure). Reached for an eXIf with a TIFF header.

subject: decoder
statement: Decoders should check the first four bytes to ensure that they have the hexadecimal values 49 49 2A 00 or 4D 4D 00 2A. Ignored otherwise. (Pointers inside the profile are not followed.)

subject: datastream
statement: The eXIf chunk contains an Exif profile: TIFF framing (TIFF 6.0 section 2), an 8-byte header whose first-IFD offset lies in the data, and that IFD's entry count, entries and next-IFD offset within it. Reference: ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: tIME: year, month, day, hour, minute, second. Reached for a well-formed tIME.

subject: datastream
statement: Month 1-12, Day 1-31, Hour 0-23, Minute 0-59, Second 0-60 (to allow for leap seconds). Ignored otherwise.

subject: datastream
statement: acTL: num_frames, num_plays. Reached for an acTL before IDAT.

subject: datastream
statement: acTL is 8 bytes (two four-byte unsigned integers). Ignored; the static image is decoded.

subject: datastream
statement: The acTL chunk must appear before the first IDAT chunk within a valid PNG stream. Ignored; the static image is decoded.

subject: datastream
statement: To be recognized as an APNG, an acTL chunk must appear in the stream before any IDAT chunks. fcTL or fdAT without one: the static image is decoded.

subject: datastream
statement: num_frames: 0 is not a valid value.

subject: datastream
statement: num_frames must equal the number of fcTL chunks; if this value does not equal the actual number of frames it should be treated as an error.

subject: datastream
statement: fcTL: sequence number, frame dimensions and offset, delay, dispose_op, blend_op. Reached for an fcTL with nonzero dimensions.

subject: datastream
statement: fcTL is 26 bytes. Ignored; the static image is decoded.

subject: datastream
statement: fcTL: One may occur before IDAT; all others shall be after IDAT.

subject: datastream
statement: width and height must be greater than zero.

subject: datastream
statement: x_offset plus width must not be greater than the IHDR width; similarly y_offset plus height must not be greater than the IHDR height.

subject: datastream
statement: Valid values for dispose_op are 0, 1 and 2.

subject: datastream
statement: Valid values for blend_op are 0 and 1.

subject: datastream
statement: The fcTL chunk corresponding to the default image: the x_offset and y_offset fields must be 0; the width and height fields must equal the corresponding fields from the IHDR chunk.

subject: datastream
statement: fdAT: sequence number and frame data, for a frame introduced by an fcTL after IDAT. Reached for such an fdAT.

subject: datastream
statement: fdAT: After IDAT. Ignored; the static image is decoded.

subject: datastream
statement: Because of the sequence number, fdAT chunks may not be of zero length; the sequence number is 4 bytes.

subject: datastream
statement: Exactly one fcTL chunk is required for each frame: an fdAT not preceded (after IDAT) by an fcTL belongs to no frame.

subject: datastream
statement: At least one fdAT chunk is required for each frame, except for the first frame, if that frame is represented by an IDAT chunk.

subject: datastream
statement: The first fcTL chunk shall contain sequence number 0, and the sequence numbers in the remaining fcTL and fdAT chunks shall be in ascending order, with no gaps or duplicates; decoders shall treat out-of-order APNG chunks as an error.

subject: datastream
statement: As 4.9.2#sequence-numbers: reached when the fcTL and fdAT sequence numbers are 0, 1, 2, ... in datastream order.

subject: decoder
statement: The static image may be included as the first frame of the animation by the presence of a single fcTL chunk before IDAT.

subject: decoder
statement: Otherwise (no fcTL before IDAT), the static image is not part of the animation.

subject: decoder
statement: A decoder which detects an error before the animation has started should display the static image. Reached when any APNG fault was found.

subject: decoder
statement: Detect errors as early as possible, recover from an error if possible, otherwise fail gracefully. (Not emitted: the philosophy behind every recover/either policy.)

subject: datastream
statement: A zlib stream has the structure CMF, FLG, [DICTID], compressed data, ADLER32: input ending inside the two header bytes. In IDAT this leaves no image data (13.1#data-short).

subject: decoder
statement: CM = 8 denotes the deflate compression method. A compliant decompressor must give an error indication if CM is not one of the values defined (only the value 8 is permitted). (For IDAT 10.1#zlib-method is checked first; reachable from zTXt, iCCP, iTXt.)

subject: datastream
statement: Values of CINFO above 7 are not allowed in this version of the specification. (For IDAT 10.1#zlib-method is checked first; reachable from zTXt, iCCP, iTXt.)

subject: datastream
statement: CINFO is the base-2 logarithm of the LZ77 window size, minus eight. Reached for a declared window smaller than 32K.

subject: decoder
statement: A distance reaches further back than the window CINFO declares (but within 32768). RFC 1950 gives no decompressor rule; zlib accepts it unless built with INFLATE_STRICT, libpng's sized window refuses it. Reference: decoded.

subject: datastream
statement: The FCHECK value must be such that CMF and FLG, when viewed as a 16-bit unsigned integer stored in MSB order (CMF*256 + FLG), is a multiple of 31.

subject: decoder
statement: When the other format does not use the preset dictionary feature, a compliant decompressor must reject any stream in which the FDICT flag is set. (For IDAT 10.1#no-preset-dictionary is checked first; reachable from zTXt, iCCP, iTXt.)

subject: datastream
statement: The compressed data is followed by ADLER32: input ending before all four bytes. In IDAT, recovered when the image data is complete (10.1#zlib-check).

subject: decoder
statement: ADLER32 contains a checksum value of the uncompressed data. A compliant decompressor must check CMF, FLG, and ADLER32, and provide an error indication if any of these have incorrect values.

subject: datastream
statement: The Huffman code for an alphabet is defined by the bit lengths of its codes; lengths that assign more codes than the bit widths hold define no prefix code.

subject: datastream
statement: The codes are Huffman codes; the RFC describes only two incomplete ones: a single distance code of one bit, and no distance codes. Reference: any other incomplete code (code-length, literal/length, or distance) is rejected, as zlib does; a lone one-bit literal/length code is accepted (rfc1951-3.2.2#one-literal-code).

subject: datastream
statement: A literal/length code holding a single one-bit code (an empty block's end-of-block) is incomplete; the RFC describes no such code, zlib (inftrees.c) and puff.c accept it. Reference: decoded, with a warning.

subject: datastream
statement: Codes that are never used (which have a bit length of zero) must not be assigned a value: the input holds a bit pattern that is no code (the unused half of a one-bit distance code, or any distance when there are none).

subject: datastream
statement: BTYPE 11 - reserved (error).

subject: datastream
statement: Blocks follow until one with BFINAL set ends: input ending before the final block does. In IDAT, recovered when the image data is complete (10.1#zlib-check).

subject: datastream
statement: A compressed data set consists of a series of blocks. Reached for more than one block.

subject: datastream
statement: A block of any type may produce no output (stored LEN 0, or only the end-of-block code). Reached for such a block.

subject: decoder
statement: A duplicated string reference may refer to a string in a previous block; i.e., the backward distance may cross one or more block boundaries.

subject: decoder
statement: The referenced string may overlap the current position (distance less than length).

subject: datastream
statement: A distance cannot refer past the beginning of the output stream.

subject: datastream
statement: Non-compressed block (BTYPE=00): bits up to the next byte boundary are ignored, then LEN, NLEN and LEN literal bytes.

subject: datastream
statement: LEN is the number of data bytes in the block. NLEN is the one's complement of LEN.

subject: datastream
statement: Length code 284 with 5 extra bits covers lengths 227-257; extra bits 31 would give 258, which the table does not list (258 is code 285). zlib accepts it. Reference: rejected.

subject: datastream
statement: Distance codes 0-29 are defined; distance codes 30-31 will never actually occur in the compressed data (they may still have code lengths, see rfc1951-3.2.7#hdist-over-30).

subject: datastream
statement: Compression with fixed Huffman codes (BTYPE=01).

subject: datastream
statement: Literal/length values 286-287 will never actually occur in the compressed data, but participate in the code construction.

subject: datastream
statement: Compression with dynamic Huffman codes (BTYPE=10).

subject: datastream
statement: 5 Bits: HLIT, # of Literal/Length codes - 257 (257 - 286). HLIT 30 or 31 (287 or 288 codes) is out of range.

subject: decoder
statement: 5 Bits: HDIST, # of Distance codes - 1 (1 - 32); a compliant decompressor must accept the full range of possible values. Reached for HDIST giving 31 or 32 codes (zlib refuses these: 'too many length or distance symbols').

subject: datastream
statement: 16: Copy the previous code length 3 - 6 times: there is no previous code length for the first one.

subject: datastream
statement: All code lengths form a single sequence of HLIT + HDIST + 258 values: a repeat running past its end.

subject: decoder
statement: The code length repeat codes can cross from HLIT + 257 to the HDIST + 1 code lengths.

subject: datastream
statement: The literal/length symbol 256 (end of data), encoded using the literal/length Huffman code: symbol 256 needs a nonzero code length.

subject: decoder
statement: If only one distance code is used, it is encoded using one bit, not zero bits; in this case there is a single code length of one, with one unused code.

subject: decoder
statement: One distance code of zero bits means that there are no distance codes used at all (the data is all literals).
